records.label: Large family with type III syndactyly
records.segregation: Linkage analysis suggested the locus maps to the chromosome 6q22-q24 ODD region
quotes: Analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly, but atypical facial features, further suggested that isolated type III syndactyly is also located in this same region of the genome.

notes.statement: Richardson et al. (2004) reported that Gja1 expression correlated with the phenotype observed in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.
quotes: Expression of Gja1 correlates with the phenotype observed in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.

notes.statement: Paznekas et al. (2003) found GJA1 (connexin 43) mutations in all 17 families with autosomal dominant oculodentodigital dysplasia that they screened. They detected 16 different missense mutations and 1 codon duplication. Syndactyly type III can occur in some cases of this syndrome.
quotes: Syndactyly type III and conductive deafness can occur in some cases, and cardiac abnormalities are observed in rare instances.
We found mutations in the GJA1 gene in all 17 families with oculodentodigital dysplasia that we screened. Sixteen different missense mutations and one codon duplication were detected.

notes.statement: Gladwin et al. (1997) studied a large family with type III syndactyly and atypical facial features. Their analysis suggested that isolated type III syndactyly maps to the same region of chromosome 6q (6q22-q24) as the oculodentodigital syndrome locus.
quotes: Analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly, but atypical facial features, further suggested that isolated type III syndactyly is also located in this same region of the genome.

notes.statement: Gladwin et al. (1997) noted that type III syndactyly occurs as part of oculodentodigital syndrome and has also been reported as an isolated entity.
quotes: Type III syndactyly, which occurs as part of ODD, has also been reported to occur as an isolated entity.

notes.statement: McKiernan and McCann (1993) reported a pedigree with 14 cases of type III syndactyly. Their analysis of the pedigree confirmed autosomal dominant inheritance, and clinical study showed variable expression.
quotes: Analysis of the pedigree confirms the autosomal dominant nature of the genetic defect, while clinical study reveals variable phenotypical expression.

notes.statement: McKiernan and McCann (1993) treated 3 affected members of the pedigree surgically. A fourth had been treated surgically elsewhere earlier by the senior author.
quotes: Three of these were treated surgically in this unit, and a fourth had previously been treated elsewhere by the senior author of this paper.

notes.statement: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) found autosomal dominant inheritance across 3 generations in a family with type III syndactyly and mild dental and facial features.
quotes: The mother and maternal grandmother were born with the same hand malformation.
Inheritance is autosomal dominant.

notes.statement: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) concluded that their family, with type III syndactyly plus small teeth, enamel hypoplasia and a thin nose but normal eyes, showed the variable expression of oculodentodigital dysplasia. They proposed that type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia form a clinical spectrum.
quotes: The present family provides evidence of the variable expression in oculodentodigital dysplasia.
Type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia: a clinical spectrum.

notes.statement: De Smet et al. (1994) stated that autosomal dominant inheritance was obvious in their cases of isolated ring and small finger syndactyly.
quotes: Autosomal dominant inheritance is obvious.

notes.statement: De Smet et al. (1994) concluded that surgery is required at a young age for syndactyly of the ring and small finger.
quotes: Surgery is required at a young age.

notes.statement: Opjordsmoen and Nyberg-Hansen (1980) reported a family from northern Norway in which 9 of 22 members across 3 generations had spastic paraplegia with neurogenic bladder disturbances and syndactyly. The bladder disturbances were the main complaint and appeared early in the disease. The authors considered the family probably to represent an unusual form of hereditary spastic paraplegia with autosomal dominant inheritance.
quotes: The bladder disturbances, being incomplete supranuclear bladder paresis (uninhibited neurogenic bladder), were the main complaint and occurred at an early stage of the disease.
The family probably represents an unusual form of hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP).

notes.statement: Brueton et al. (1990) described a family with type III syndactyly and facies resembling the facial phenotype of oculodentodigital dysplasia, without any of the other characteristic findings of oculodentodigital dysplasia, and discussed whether the two conditions are separate genetic entities or part of a disease spectrum.
quotes: A family is described with type III syndactyly and facies resembling the oculodentodigital dysplasia facial phenotype in the absence of any of the other characteristic findings of the latter condition.
The relationship between type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia is discussed.
